objectClass.notes: Three admitted complementary views describe the same clean stylized temple prop. The front view fixes facade symmetry and explicitly solar—not Christian—iconography; the side fixes nave length, five-lancet rhythm, roof volume, and rear tower placement; the three-quarter view fixes depth and attachments. Hidden rear/left details are continued conservatively by symmetry. This is a stylized procedural reconstruction, not survey geometry or photoreal inverse rendering.

reasoning: The identity silhouette combines a long nave, raised front gable, columned portico, rear-offset square tower, tall slate spire, and radial sun finial.
The roof must be a closed solid gable volume with attached shingle relief, never two rotated box slabs.
The facade requires a large rose window, a separate gold sun disc, twin pointed lancets, recessed doors, four columns, a pediment, and stepped plinth.
Repeated systems include ashlar courses, slate courses, side buttresses, side lancets, glass leading, rose wedges, belfry openings, spire ribs, sun rays, and column modules.
Three distinct views substantially reduce occlusion risk; the rear elevation and exact hidden roof/tower intersection remain inferred.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The outer building mass is simple, but identity depends on a deep architectural hierarchy, two solar emblems, repeated stained-glass systems, and an attached multi-stage steeple.

resolvedAssumptions: Rear wall openings remain restrained because no rear view was supplied.
The left nave elevation mirrors the admitted right-side five-lancet rhythm.
Slate and ashlar relief remain regular and stylized rather than photoreal micro-noise.

detailInventory.note: Twenty observed identity systems are consolidated from the main, front, and side scans. Every item maps to a concrete component.localFeatures or material.localOverrides entry used by the sculpt spec.

details.description: A rear-offset square tower rises into an open belfry, tall dark faceted spire, gold cap, stem, and radial sun finial.
A gold circular solar core with alternating long and short radial rays crowns the spire; no cross geometry is present.
Tall dark recessed arches appear on each belfry face between white stone corner piers.
Thin gold vertical ribs and a lower diamond lattice sit proud of the dark slate spire.
The long nave roof is one closed gable prism with triangular end caps, eaves, and continuous ridge.
Regular dark-blue slate courses overlap across both roof pitches with a restrained alternating value pattern.
Offset rectangular white stone blocks form regular shallow courses with cool grey recessed mortar lines.
The large circular rose window uses a gold central sun, sixteen gold rays, and saturated radial stained-glass wedges.
Dark radial lead cames divide the colored rose wedges and a thick dark ring separates glass from the white stone frame.
A separate gold sun disc with embossed concentric center and alternating pointed rays sits below the rose window; it is explicitly not a cross.
Four white columns use tapered shafts, square plinths, neck rings, and stepped capitals under a deep entablature.
The portico roof is a shallow closed gable/pediment volume with a white face and gold inner trim.
Four broad shallow stone steps widen toward ground level and terminate the facade at y=0.
Two tall narrow pointed stained-glass lancets flank the raised central facade.
Five evenly spaced tall pointed lancets repeat along each nave side between slim projecting buttress piers.
Each lancet contains a small gold sun, blue-violet upper fields, green chevrons, red lower diamond, and dark geometric lead cames.
Thin warm-gold bands trace the nave eaves, front wing shoulders, belfry cap, and portico pediment.
Slim white projecting vertical piers divide the nave bays and terminate in a continuous raised base course.
A dark recessed double doorway sits behind the portico, separated by a narrow center seam and white stone reveal.
Exposed stone corners, trims, frames, steps, and column blocks use small real chamfers that catch the upper-left key light.

definitionOfDone: The model reads immediately as the admitted fantasy sun temple from front, side, and three-quarter views.
The tall rear-offset steeple, dark solid spire, gold radial sun finial, white ashlar, rose-window sun, separate facade sun disc, portico, steps, and repeated lancets all survive.
Every structural roof is a closed solid prism or faceted solid; no dual rotated box-slab roof construction is permitted.
The palette remains bright and clean with geometric stone/slate relief and no photoreal micro-noise or reference-image billboard.

featureGroups.name: Nave, raised facade, rear steeple, spire, and sun-finial silhouette
qualityCriteria: The long nave and tall rear-offset steeple preserve the front/side/three-quarter proportions.
The sun finial is radial solar geometry and cannot read as a cross.

featureGroups.name: Closed solid slate roof and spire volumes
qualityCriteria: The nave and portico roofs are closed gable prisms with end caps and continuous ridges.
Slate tiles are surface relief only; they are never used as two structural rotated box slabs.

featureGroups.name: Rose-window sun and separate golden facade sun emblem
qualityCriteria: The rose contains a gold sun core, radial rays, saturated colored wedges, dark lead spokes, and a white stone surround.
The lower gold emblem is a distinct raised sun disc with pointed rays and no Christian cross.

featureGroups.name: Columned portico, solid pediment, recessed doors, and broad steps
qualityCriteria: Four attached columns carry a deep entablature and closed gable pediment.
The entry steps widen downward, touch y=0, and lead to a dark recessed double door.

featureGroups.name: Ashlar, buttress, and stained-glass lancet rhythm
qualityCriteria: Five pointed windows repeat along each nave side and two flank the front facade.
White buttress piers and ashlar courses create shallow real relief between saturated glass panels.

featureGroups.name: Clean stylized stone, slate, gold, glass, lead, and wood response
qualityCriteria: Material blocks are bright and readable under neutral light with separate roughness roles.
Stone and slate use restrained macro/meso/micro variation through geometry and scalar response, not photoreal image noise.
Gold remains warm and metallic; stained glass remains saturated but opaque enough for a toon/game-prop renderer.

featureGroups.name: Attachment, pivot, collider, socket, and destruction readiness
qualityCriteria: Spire, finial, emblems, portico, windows, and doors have stable named parent pivots and no visible gaps.
Runtime metadata exposes door hinges, sockets, primitive colliders, and semantic destruction groups.

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed if any identity feature is represented only by prose.
Do not proceed if either roof is modeled as two rotated box slabs.
Do not proceed if the gold finial or facade emblem can read as a Christian cross.
Do not proceed if the rose window is a single unsegmented colored disc.
Do not proceed if side lancets, buttresses, ashlar, or slate courses lack repeated systems.
Do not proceed if attached steeple, portico, window, or door assemblies lack parent/contact data.
Do not pass material look-dev if white stone, slate, gold, glass, lead, and wood collapse into a muddy palette.
Do not claim photoreal PBR extraction or photo billboards for this accepted stylized solid-color target.
